reconcile.note: Gill distinguishes two senses of divine fatherhood: God is Father of all humanity by creation, but Father of believers in the narrower sense of adoption through grace.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Harnack argued the universal fatherhood of God was the authentic core of Jesus' teaching, treating its later restriction to believers as a narrowing of that message.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Adolf von Harnack (1900), What Is Christianity?

sides.snippet: All of you are sons of the Most High
sides.verseText: I said, \"You are gods, All of you are sons of the Most High.

sides.snippet: For you are all children of God, through faith in Christ Jesus.
sides.verseText: For you are all children of God, through faith in Christ Jesus.
